neighbours.label: a noun naming a piece of research as the subject about to be described ('The [study] followed…', 'The [report] found…', 'The current [study] was…') in science reporting; not 'study' as a verb or a room
fire: Dark chocolate may protect the heart, according to new findings. The study tracked 8,000 nurses over two decades.
Night-shift workers sleep worse even on their days off. The survey covered more than 3,000 hospital staff.
Earlier work had hinted at a link between gum disease and dementia; the study confirms it in a larger group.
Bees can count to four, scientists say. The research was carried out at a field station in Bavaria.
Children who walk to school concentrate better in class. The report draws on data from twelve countries.
Until now nobody knew how the virus entered the cell; the present study shows that it uses a sugar receptor.
Regular naps were linked to lower blood pressure. The analysis included adults aged forty to seventy.
Urban foxes are getting bolder, a team in Bristol says. The study relied on 500 camera traps.
quiet: My brother wants to study the effect of dark chocolate on the hearts of nurses.
Night-shift workers were asked to report how badly they slept on their days off.

Children who walk to school concentrate better in class. Teachers in twelve countries agree.

notes: Card: ' study' is 22 of the top 32 peaks, always 'The study' / 'the current study' opening a statement about research; the output direction suppresses ' study' and promotes ' involving', ' found', ' conducted'. Probes: 'The study followed' 0.74, 'The current study was' 0.49, and 'The report followed' 0.74, so it is not the token alone; 'to study for her exam' 0.03, 'a study with a desk' 0.04. Near misses: 'study'/'report' in other senses, and the same findings with people as subject.
